From 7bca405c986075c99b9f729d3587b5c45db39d01 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Lucas Stach <l.stach@pengutronix.de>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2024 19:50:26 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] bus: imx-weim: fix valid range check

When the range parsing was open-coded the number of u32 entries to
parse had to be a multiple of 4 and the driver checks this. With
the range parsing converted to the range parser the counting changes
from individual u32 entries to a complete range, so the check must
not reject counts not divisible by 4.

Fixes: 2a88e4792c6d ("bus: imx-weim: Remove open coded "ranges" parsing")
Signed-off-by: Lucas Stach <l.stach@pengutronix.de>
Signed-off-by: Shawn Guo <shawnguo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c b/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c
index 6b5da73c8541..837bf9d51c6e 100644
--- a/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c
+++ b/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c
@@ -120,7 +120,7 @@ static int imx_weim_gpr_setup(struct platform_device *pdev)
 		i++;
 	}
 
-	if (i == 0 || i % 4)
+	if (i == 0)
 		goto err;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(gprvals); i++) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/bus/imx-weim.c`**
- The condition that checks the count of parsed entries has been modified. 
- The original check `if (i == 0 || i % 4)` has been changed to `if (i == 0)`. 
- This change removes the requirement that the count of entries (`i`) must be a multiple of 4, allowing for more flexibility in the number of entries parsed.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `2a88e4792c6d`) that changed the way ranges were parsed. The original implementation required the number of entries to be a multiple of 4, which was appropriate for the open-coded parsing method. However, with the new range parser, this requirement is no longer valid, necessitating the change to ensure that valid counts are accepted regardless of divisibility by 4.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
for_each_of_range(&parser, &range) {
    ...
    i++;
}
```
```c
if (i == 0 || i % 4)
```
Reason:
The loop counts the number of ranges parsed into `i`, but the subsequent check incorrectly enforces that `i` must be a multiple of 4. This was valid in the previous implementation but became invalid after switching to the range parser, which allows for any valid number of entries.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (i == 0)
```
Reason:
The fix removes the requirement that `i` must be a multiple of 4, allowing the function to accept any valid count of parsed ranges, thus aligning the validation with the new range parsing logic.
